issues: Wrong law and year for the slice's definition ('first comprehensive law'). The 2015 Law on Personal Data Protection (ՀՕ-49-Ն) was not Armenia's first general data-protection statute. The Law 'On Personal Data' ('Անհատական տվյալների մասին', ՀՕ-422-Ն) was adopted by the National Assembly on 8 October 2002, signed on 7 November 2002 and in force from 14 February 2003.

The 2002 law was general, not sectoral. Article 1 applies it to processing by state and local self-government bodies, state or community institutions, and legal or natural persons. It was repealed by Article 30(2) of the 2015 law with effect from 1 July 2015. Both texts were read on ARLIS, Armenia's official legal information system.

The DLA Piper source is accurate but describes only the 2015 successor law, which has been moved into the note. It was adopted on 18 May 2015 and in force from 1 July 2015 (ARLIS: 'Սույն օրենքն ուժի մեջ է մտնում 2015 թվականի հուլիսի 1-ից').

The id 'am-2015' no longer matches the year. It has been left unchanged so that this verdict still applies, but the editorial layer may rename it to am-2002. Any per-decade counts built from the laws table should move Armenia from the 2010s to the 2000s.
Coordinates (40.1813, 44.5144) are central Yerevan (the capital), which the slice convention allows.

The National Assembly adopted it on 8 October 2002 and it came into force on 14 February 2003. It covered processing by state and local self-government bodies, state and community institutions, and legal and natural persons. It was repealed and replaced by the Law on Personal Data Protection (ՀՕ-49-Ն) of 18 May 2015, which came into force on 1 July 2015.
